chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

He was asked about the mutamatti', how much suffices him. He said: one sheep. And I asked him about the enslaved mutamatti', so he said: upon him is the like of what is upon the free man, either a sacrifice or fasting.

The proper way of understanding this report is one of several possibilities. One of them is that this is informing of his equality to the free man in the amount of what is due upon him, even if what is binding regarding the enslaved person, by way of choice, rests with his master; for if he wishes, he offers a sacrificial animal on his behalf, and if he wishes, he instructs him to fast. If he instructs him to fast, then what is binding upon him of fasting is the same as what is binding upon the free man, namely fasting ten days. This is not treated like zihar, in which half of what is binding upon the free man is binding upon him. Likewise, if he wishes to slaughter on his behalf, it is binding upon him to offer on his behalf the like of what is offered on behalf of the free man. From this aspect he is like the free man, not from the standpoint of the sacrificial offering being initially obligatory upon him.

The second possibility is that it is to be understood regarding one who was enslaved and then emancipated before missing either of the two standing-places; then the sacrificial offering becomes binding upon him, because he reached the hajj while he was free, so what is binding upon the free man becomes binding upon him, according to what has previously been stated concerning it.

And the third is that if the master does not instruct his slave to fast until the final departure, then it becomes binding upon him to slaughter on his behalf, and fasting does not suffice him. That is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: the two ritual standing-places of hajj
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: the sacrificial animal due in hajj
key_terms.شَاةٌ: one sheep as the sufficient sacrificial animal
key_terms.صَوْمٌ: fasting as an alternative expiation here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the sacrificial offering or fasting of an enslaved person performing hajj al-tamattu'?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of the sacrificial obligation for the mutamatti' in hajj, including the case of an enslaved person who performs tamattu' with his master's permission. The text explains several ways to reconcile the report, focusing on whether the enslaved person matches the free person in the amount due, the master's role in choosing sacrifice or fasting, and the case of emancipation before the rites are missed.
